subject: chopping onion
title: What If Onions Didn't Make You Cry?

scenes.text: What if onions never made you cry? The onion would have to stop defending itself.
An onion stores its chemical weapons in separate compartments. Your knife smashes them together.
Two enzymes then build a gas called syn-propanethial S-oxide, the onion's tear gas.
It turns to vapour almost instantly, drifts up, and hits the water on your eyes.
Your nerves sense the irritation and flood your eyes with tears to wash it out.
Scientists found the second enzyme in two thousand two. Breeders have since grown onions that barely fight back.

description:
What if onions didn't make you cry? Cutting an onion mixes compounds that enzymes turn into syn-propanethial S-oxide, a volatile gas that irritates the nerves in your eyes.
Japanese researchers identified the key enzyme, lachrymatory-factor synthase, in 2002. Since then, crossbred 'tearless' onions such as Sunions have reached shops.
